text:
Viktor Arvidsson started his first season in Detroit fast, including a hat trick against Chicago on Oct 29, and Octopus Thrower wrote that the numbers back up his play. Since then the Red Wings have hit a wall and so has he: no goals in eight games and no points in six.

The goal drought is the kind that ends. He's taking 1.54 expected goals per 60 on his own shots, up from last season's 1.35, and he has 8 goals on 10.0 expected. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 99th percentile for chances from the slot last season and carrying the puck in on 58% of his entries. He goes to the net, and pucks follow players who go there.

The other numbers are flatter. Detroit takes 49% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on ice, a little below the team rate, and his linemates' chances have thinned over the six-game point drought. Evolving-Hockey had him 47th among forwards in wins above replacement last season. Our talent range still projects about 33 goals. With Dylan Larkin's situation hanging over Detroit, the Red Wings need his finishing back soon.
